claims.text: Severe plastic deformation followed by tailored aging will improve the combined strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance of high-entropy alloys relative to conventional processing.
Conventionally melted or rapidly solidified high-entropy alloys typically begin as single-phase random solid solutions.
Controlled severe plastic deformation will refine the grain structure.
Tailored aging after severe plastic deformation will produce coherent nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates.
The two-step treatment will create a fine-grained matrix containing uniformly dispersed coherent nanoprecipitates.
Grain refinement caused by severe plastic deformation enhances strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
Severe-plastic-deformation-induced grain refinement promotes homogeneous deformation and thereby improves ductility.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates impede dislocation motion and increase strength.
Coherent nanoscale precipitates can increase strength without sacrificing ductility.
The precipitate-containing microstructure enhances fracture resistance.
The coherent precipitates provide a reinforcing contribution that increases Young’s modulus.
The processed alloy will exhibit higher yield strength and ultimate tensile strength than a conventionally processed control.
The processed alloy will exhibit greater uniform elongation than a conventionally processed control.
The processed alloy will exhibit a higher Young’s modulus than a conventionally processed control.
The processed alloy will exhibit improved fracture-toughness or impact-resistance metrics relative to a conventionally processed control.
The approach is expected to work only for compositions and aging conditions that permit controlled formation of coherent precipitates.
Deleterious phase separation, incoherent interfaces, coarse precipitates, excessive residual stress, unstable phases, or strain-induced damage can prevent the proposed improvements.
A successful treatment should produce at least a 20% statistically significant increase in yield strength together with improvements in ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance.
